name: John Waller
description: John Waller, known before his conversion as Swearing Jack, became a leading Separate Baptist preacher who was jailed repeatedly in several Virginia county jails for unlicensed preaching, accumulating roughly 113 days of imprisonment. He was first confined at the Spotsylvania County jail in Fredericksburg in June 1768 alongside Lewis Craig and others.
charges: Preaching without a license and disturbing the peace
sentence: About 43 days confinement in Spotsylvania, part of roughly 113 days total across several jails

name: James Childs
description: James Childs, also recorded as Chiles, was a Separate Baptist preacher seized with John Waller and Lewis Craig for unlicensed preaching in Spotsylvania County. He was jailed at Fredericksburg in June 1768 and held with the group for about six weeks.
charges: Preaching without a license and disturbing the peace

name: William Marsh
description: William Marsh, whose name also appears as Mash, was among the Separate Baptist preachers arrested for unlicensed preaching in Spotsylvania County in 1768. He was confined at the Fredericksburg jail with John Waller and the others for roughly six weeks.
charges: Preaching without a license and disturbing the peace

name: Joseph Craig
description: Joseph Craig, brother of the preachers Lewis and Elijah Craig, was a Separate Baptist repeatedly harassed and jailed for unlicensed preaching. He was confined in the Caroline County jail in the early 1770s before being released.
charges: Preaching without a license and disturbing the peace

name: John Weatherford
description: John Weatherford was a Baptist preacher held in the Chesterfield County jail for about five months in 1773 and 1774 for unlicensed preaching. Patrick Henry is traditionally credited with aiding his release.
charges: Preaching without a license and disturbing the peace

name: John Shackelford
description: John Shackelford was a Separate Baptist preacher jailed for unlicensed preaching during the Middlesex County prosecutions around 1771. He was confined at the Urbanna jail before being released.
charges: Preaching without a license and disturbing the peace

name: William Webber
description: William Webber was a Separate Baptist preacher imprisoned for unlicensed preaching in Chesterfield and Middlesex counties. He was among the ministers confined for the offense in 1768 and later at Urbanna.
charges: Preaching without a license and disturbing the peace

name: Joseph Anthony
description: Joseph Anthony was a Baptist preacher confined in the Chesterfield County jail for unlicensed preaching in 1768. He was released after his term of confinement.
charges: Preaching without a license and disturbing the peace

name: David Tinsley
description: David Tinsley was a Baptist preacher confined in the Chesterfield County jail in 1774 for unlicensed preaching, where he was held for several months. He continued to preach to gathered crowds through the jail window before his release.
charges: Preaching without a license and disturbing the peace

name: Caesar (John Vaarck)
description: Enslaved man owned by John Vaarck, jailed in early 1741 after the Hogg robbery and held in the City Hall jail; the court treated him as a principal in the alleged plot and hanged him first.
charges: Burglary in the Hogg robbery and alleged conspiracy to burn New York City

name: Prince (John Auboyneau)
description: Enslaved man owned by John Auboyneau, jailed alongside Caesar over the same robbery and hanged as an alleged ringleader of the plot.
charges: Burglary in the Hogg robbery and alleged conspiracy to burn New York City

name: Quack (John Roosevelt)
description: Enslaved man owned by John Roosevelt, accused of setting the fire at Fort George and burned at the stake despite an alibi given by his owner.
charges: Arson at Fort George and conspiracy to burn New York City
sentence: Death by burning at the stake

name: Cuffee (Adolph Philipse)
description: Enslaved man owned by Adolph Philipse, convicted of conspiracy and burned at the stake alongside Quack before a large crowd.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City and murder its inhabitants
sentence: Death by burning at the stake

name: Cato (John Cowley)
description: Enslaved man owned by John Cowley, condemned as one of the so-called inferior agents of the alleged plot and burned at the stake.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City
sentence: Death by burning at the stake

name: Fortune (Vanderspiegle)
description: Enslaved man owned by Vanderspiegle, burned at the stake as one of five agents executed together in mid June.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City
sentence: Death by burning at the stake

name: Cato (Provoost)
description: Enslaved man owned by Provoost, also known as Toby, burned at the stake as an alleged conspirator among the five agents.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City
sentence: Death by burning at the stake

name: Ben (Captain Marshall)
description: Enslaved man owned by Captain Marshall, burned at the stake among the five agents executed together in June.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City
sentence: Death by burning at the stake

name: Quash (Rutgers)
description: Enslaved man owned by Rutgers, burned at the stake as an alleged conspirator among the five agents.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City
sentence: Death by burning at the stake

name: Othello (Chief Justice)
description: Enslaved man owned by Chief Justice James De Lancey, hanged for alleged participation in the plot after refusing to plead guilty.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City

name: Quack
description: Enslaved man hanged as an alleged conspirator among the group executed on the same day as Doctor Harry; distinct from the Quack burned in May.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City

name: Venture
description: Enslaved man hanged as an alleged conspirator in the July group executed with Othello.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City

name: Frank
description: Enslaved man hanged as an alleged conspirator on the same day as Othello and Doctor Harry.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City

name: Fortune
description: Enslaved man hanged as an alleged conspirator in the July group; distinct from the Fortune burned at the stake in June.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City

name: Galloway
description: Enslaved man hanged as an alleged conspirator in the July group executed alongside Othello.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City

name: Harry
description: Enslaved healer known as Doctor Harry who had earlier been banished from the city; burned at the stake as an alleged conspirator on the same day as the July hangings.
charges: Conspiracy to burn New York City
sentence: Death by burning at the stake

name: John Hughson
description: White tavern keeper whose alehouse was named as the meeting place of the alleged plot; held in the City Hall jail and hanged, with his body later left in chains.
charges: Conspiracy and receiving stolen goods in the alleged plot to burn New York City

name: Sarah Hughson
description: Wife of tavern keeper John Hughson, convicted as a conspirator and hanged with him on the same day.
charges: Conspiracy in the alleged plot to burn New York City

name: Margaret Kerry
description: Irish woman known as Peggy Kerry or Sorubiero who lodged at the Hughson tavern; hanged as an alleged conspirator alongside the Hughsons.
charges: Conspiracy and receiving stolen goods in the alleged plot

name: John Ury
description: Schoolmaster accused of being a Catholic priest and a leader of the plot; held in the City Hall jail and hanged in late August, the last person executed.
charges: Conspiracy and being a Catholic priest inciting the alleged plot
